chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim, from Hasan ibn 'Ali, from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

If a woman sees blood at the beginning of her first menstruation, and the blood continues with her after that, she leaves the salat (prayer) for ten days, then performs salat (prayer) for twenty days. If the blood continues with her after that, she leaves the salat (prayer) for three days and performs salat (prayer) for twenty-seven days.
Hasan ibn 'Ali said, and Ibn Bukayr said: This is among the matters from which they find no alternative.

key_terms.الدَّمَ: the blood seen by the woman
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman subject to this legal ruling
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ: three days, the later recurring period of leaving salat (prayer)
key_terms.عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ: ten days, the first period of leaving salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman whose bleeding continues from the first time she menstruates?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a woman who sees menstrual blood for the first time and then experiences continuous bleeding. It outlines how she is to alternate between leaving salat (prayer) and performing it according to specified day-counts, establishing a practical fiqh ruling for ongoing blood discharge.
